title: Meeting Louis Armstrong at the Earle Theater; biggest trumpet sounds
summary: Stewart first met Armstrong in 1938 on a Philadelphia bill and thinks Armstrong had the greatest trumpet sound, above Hot Lips Page, Red Allen and Eldridge.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Did you ever work with Louis Armstrong?
I worked on the same show with Louis and his group. That was back in 1938, when Slim and I were doing theaters. As a matter of fact, this goes back or we go

down to Philadelphia -- no, let's see now. Let me think. Yes, we were playing in -- at the Earle Theater in Philadelphia and Louie Armstrong and his band had the top billing and Slim and I were on the same show and that's the first time I had the opportunity to even meet Louie in person. We never did play together on this particular show. I sat in with Louie on other occasions, but that was it for the first time, Louie Armstrong.
Was he playing all those high C's at the end?
Yes, he was. Yes, he was. And it was amazing to me, yeah.
Yeah, he did have incredible stamina.

Which -- like we mentioned earlier, like big sounds like -- on the saxophone like Don Byas, Coleman Hawkins, Ben Webster, who were the guys who stick out in your mind as having the biggest sound for trumpet that you played with or that you heard play?
That I heard. Well, of course, Louie -- I think Louis had about the greatest sound and out of the trumpet players whom I just mentioned, Hot Lips.
He had a beautiful sound. Red Allen. And, of course, let's not forget Little Jazz, what I mean, Roy
Eldridge, what I mean. He was very powerful on that trumpet.
But you think Armstrong had him though, as far as the power.
The power. I think he was the tops, yeah.
